samples.text:
The table shows the number of new books which was published in six different genres in one country in 2004, 2014 and 2024.

Fiction was the most popular genre in all three years. It increased from 11,200 books in 2004 to 14,800 in 2014 and 17,900 in 2024. Children's books was the second, and they also went up from 6,500 to 8,900 and then 10,100.

Self-help books increased very fast. In 2004 there were only 1,300 books but it rose to 3,400 in 2014 and 5,800 in 2024, so it became the third biggest genre at the end.

On the other hand, some genres decreased. Science and technology books fell from 4,800 to 4,200 and 3,900. Travel books had the biggest fall, from 2,100 to 1,500 and only 900 in 2024. Biography was a bit different, because it rose from 2,900 to 3,100 in 2014 but then it drop to 2,600 in 2024.

Overall, fiction, children's and self-help books was increasing, but travel and science books was decreasing.
samples.why: Accurate figures with rising and falling genres grouped · overview basic and placed at the end · limited, repetitive trend vocabulary · agreement and verb-form errors that do not impede meaning.

samples.text:
The table illustrates how many new titles were published in six genres in one country in 2004, 2014 and 2024.

Overall, fiction was by far the largest genre throughout the period, and it grew considerably, as did children's books and self-help. By contrast, the number of new travel and science and technology titles declined, while biography remained relatively stable.

Fiction titles rose steadily from 11,200 in 2004 to 14,800 in 2014, reaching 17,900 in 2024. Children's books followed a similar upward trend, increasing from 6,500 to 10,100 over the twenty years. However, the most remarkable growth was seen in self-help books, which more than quadrupled from just 1,300 to 5,800, making self-help the third largest genre by the end of the period.

In contrast, the number of science and technology titles fell gradually from 4,800 to 3,900. Travel saw the sharpest decline, with new publications dropping from 2,100 to 1,500 in 2014 and to just 900 in 2024, less than half the original figure. The figures for biography fluctuated slightly, rising from 2,900 to 3,100 before falling back to 2,600.
samples.why: Clear overview of growing and shrinking genres · key features highlighted with accurate multiples · logical paragraphing · good range of trend vocabulary · mostly error-free, with one clumsy noun phrase.

samples.text:
The table shows the number of new books published in six genres in one country at ten-year intervals between 2004 and 2024.

The most notable trend is the divergence between genres: fiction, children's books and self-help all expanded markedly, whereas output of science and technology and travel titles contracted. Fiction remained the dominant genre throughout, while self-help recorded by far the fastest growth.

New fiction titles increased by 6,700 over the two decades, from 11,200 to 17,900, consolidating their leading position. Children's books, the second largest category, also rose substantially, from 6,500 to 10,100. Most striking of all, however, was the surge in self-help publishing: from a modest 1,300 titles in 2004, the smallest figure in the table, output climbed to 3,400 in 2014 and 5,800 in 2024, overtaking first biography and then science and technology.

The remaining genres moved in the opposite direction. Science and technology titles fell steadily from 4,800 to 3,900, while travel publishing more than halved, sinking from 2,100 to just 900. Biography was the only genre to fluctuate, edging up from 2,900 to 3,100 before slipping to 2,600, slightly below its starting level.
samples.why: Clear overview of diverging trends · key features skilfully selected, including changes in rank · cohesion seamless · wide, precise vocabulary (consolidating, contracted) · wide range of structures, error-free.
